problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Suppose that $X∼N(\mu ,{5.5}^{2})$ and $P(X\le 18.2)=0.5871.$ Find $\mu .$ Use the table below and do not round your answer.

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.1\,$ | $\,0.5398\,$ | $\,0.5438\,$ | $\,0.5478\,$ |
| $\,0.2\,$ | $\,0.5793\,$ | $\,0.5832\,$ | $\,0.5871\,$ |
| $\,0.3\,$ | $\,0.6179\,$ | $\,0.6217\,$ | $\,0.6255\,$ |

$\mu =$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
First, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 18.2) & =0.5871 \\ P(Z\le \frac{18.2-\mu }{5.5}) & =0.5871 \\ Φ(\frac{18.2-\mu }{5.5}) & =0.5871 \\ \frac{18.2-\mu }{5.5} & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.5871)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(0.22)=0.5871\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.5871)=0.22.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{18.2-\mu }{5.5} & =0.22 \\ 18.2-\mu  & =1.21 \\ \mu  & =16.99.\end{aligned}
$$
